summary: A $^{133}$Cs optical tweezer array enclosed in a 4 K radiation shield achieves Rydberg lifetimes of $406(36)$ μs for the $55P_{3/2}$ state, a factor of $3.3(3)$ longer than room temperature, by suppressing blackbody radiation-induced transitions to an effective temperature below 25 K. Single-photon excitation and small differential light-shift coefficient $ m eta = 29(15)$ kHz/MHz$^2$ enable coherent ground-Rydberg qubit control with $T_2^* = 6.2(4)$ μs and project $T_1$ contribution to two-qubit gate infidelity down to $1.6 	imes 10^{-4}$ at optimized Rabi frequency.
motivation: Two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom arrays now exceed 99.7%, making $T_1$ relaxation from Rydberg spontaneous emission and blackbody radiation the dominant error source; suppressing the latter via cryogenic environment offers a pathway to further improvement.
method: Cesium atoms are loaded into optical tweezers inside nested 4 K and 35 K radiation shields with ITO-coated windows to attenuate microwave blackbody radiation; ground-Rydberg qubits are manipulated via single-photon UV excitation at 319 nm; lifetimes are measured by two-pulse sequences with pushout of decay products.
result: The $55P_{3/2}$ lifetime extends from $122$ μs at room temperature to $406(36)$ μs at cryogenic temperature, suppressing BBR-induced decay by more than one order of magnitude and approaching the spontaneous-decay limit of $429$ μs; projected $T_1$-limited gate infidelity drops from $(1$–$3) 	imes 10^{-3}$ to $1.6 	imes 10^{-4}$ at beam waist $20$ μm.
